observations: Neet has four grounded fine limbs, continuous full narrow trunk, broad upright ears and tiny nub. His bread piece remains at the mouth. Buddy has continuous shoulder-to-hip mass, two forepaws bracketing the muzzle and two folded hind paws; belly/chin and paws visibly contact the tile.
Buddy’s torso contour is smooth and its low-contrast wash does not create raised shag volume. Furnished beard, brows and hanging ears remain regional. Neet’s short coat retains a smooth silhouette.

The offered roti, stationary Buddy under the fan, Neet’s acquired bite and Heather laughing beside her laptop give distinct readable parts of the joke. Warm afternoon kitchen/living space agrees with the anchor. Human likeness is provisional.

Neet’s four standing feet are separated and grounded; his head directs attention to the escaped ball. Buddy’s visible bent foreleg and paired folded hindfeet connect to shoulder and pelvis; his far foreleg is occluded beneath the head/chest, with no orphan limb. Supported side-set rest is physically plausible.

The clear gap between Buddy and the lattice ball communicates the failed trap; fallen cushion and evening lighting support the action. The pause reads more quietly than the accident itself, consistent with this post-action anchor.

Actual v005 replacement and native concern crop x850–1375/y410–675 inspected. Charcoal flank and back are now broad soft shading, with no conspicuous repeated engraved strands. Very faint low-contrast surface traces on the upper leg do not create curls, raised contour or added coat volume. Regional ear/beard/paw furnishings remain. Four grounded Neet feet, folded Buddy legs, independent ball and scene state survive the edit.

The sleeping dogs remain separate continuous bodies. Neet’s near foreleg reaches over the ball, far foreleg lies behind its lower-left edge, and two hindfeet arise from his folded pelvis. Buddy’s near foreleg reaches from the shoulder onto the same ball, with the other foreleg occluded; two hindfeet connect to his right-side hip. Heads and trunks are supported on the rug.

Closed eyes, touching forepaws and the single orange lattice ball deliver affectionate shared custody after competitive play. The beige sofa/fallen cushion and night window preserve scene continuity without introducing humans or a new incident.

Actual v005 replacement and native concern crop x680–1340/y340–570 inspected. Flank and shoulder now have broad continuous shading instead of repeated curved incisions; upper back contour is smooth. Remaining fine strands belong to the back of the furnished head/ear region, not a shagged torso. Separate supported bodies and the traceable forepaws around one ball remain intact.
